title: Beta: Set up staging environment on Railway and Vercel
body:
## Overview
Set up a dedicated staging environment that mirrors production, to be used for private beta testing. This must be completely isolated from any future production environment.

## Tasks
- [ ] Create a separate Railway project for staging (staging API + staging PostgreSQL + staging Redis)
- [ ] Create a separate Vercel project for staging web and admin apps
- [ ] Configure staging environment variables (separate Paystack test keys, separate Smile ID sandbox, separate Termii test account)
- [ ] Set up staging branch in GitHub (`staging`) that auto-deploys to staging environments via existing CI/CD workflows
- [ ] Add staging-specific seed script that creates realistic test groups, members, and cycles
- [ ] Confirm Paystack test mode works end to end in staging (test card charges, test transfers)
- [ ] Add staging banner to web and admin UI so testers are always aware they are on staging

## Acceptance criteria
- Merging to `staging` branch auto-deploys all apps to staging environments
- Paystack test transactions work end to end in staging without touching real money
- Staging DB is fully isolated from any production data
- Staging URL is accessible to invited beta testers

title: Beta: Recruit and onboard private beta testers
body:
## Overview
Recruit a small, trusted group of real users for the private beta. The goal is to put real-world human behaviour through the app before public launch.

## Target beta group profile
- 2-3 complete Ajo groups (8-10 members each)
- Mix of segments: at least one market/trader group and one friend/individual group
- At least one group with real NGN contributions (even a small amount like 1,000 per person) to test real Paystack flows
- Testers should be people willing to give honest feedback, not just friends who will be polite

## Tasks
- [ ] Define beta tester criteria and write a simple onboarding brief explaining what they are testing and what to expect
- [ ] Set up a feedback channel (WhatsApp group or simple Tally/Google Form) for testers to report bugs and suggestions
- [ ] Recruit at least 2 complete groups (16-20 testers total)
- [ ] Onboard testers: walk them through registration, KYC, and group setup
- [ ] Run at least 2 full contribution cycles per group during beta
- [ ] Collect structured feedback at the end of beta on: trust in the platform, clarity of the UI, any bugs or unexpected behaviour

## Acceptance criteria
- At least 2 complete groups have completed at least 1 full cycle (all members contribute, payout is received by the correct recipient)
- All critical bugs discovered during beta are filed as GitHub issues and triaged
- A beta retrospective document is written summarising findings before public launch

title: Beta: End-to-end payment flow testing with real Paystack transactions
body:
## Overview
Run real money through the full Paystack contribution and payout flow during beta to validate reliability before public launch.

## Test scenarios to validate
- [ ] Member initiates contribution via Paystack checkout - charge succeeds, contribution marked PAID
- [ ] Member initiates contribution via Paystack checkout - charge fails, contribution remains PENDING, member is notified
- [ ] All members in a cycle pay, payout scheduler triggers on due date, recipient receives money in Poolr Wallet
- [ ] Recipient manually withdraws payout from Poolr Wallet to bank account via Paystack transfer
- [ ] Member pays contribution from Poolr Wallet balance (wallet-funded path)
- [ ] Member misses contribution - penalty engine applies penalty the next day
- [ ] Paystack transfer to recipient fails - admin is notified, retry is triggered
- [ ] Duplicate Paystack webhook is received - confirmed safely ignored (idempotency)

## Tasks
- [ ] Run each test scenario above manually with real testers
- [ ] Document the result of each scenario (pass/fail, any unexpected behaviour)
- [ ] File a GitHub issue for every failure
- [ ] Confirm Paystack dashboard reconciles with Poolr DB records for every transaction
- [ ] Confirm all webhook events are logged and traceable in Sentry

## Acceptance criteria
- All 8 test scenarios pass without data inconsistency
- Zero cases of wallet balance out of sync with WalletTransaction log
- Sentry captures any unhandled exceptions during test runs
- Paystack dashboard and Poolr DB agree on transaction status for every test transaction

title: Beta: Bug triage, fixes, and regression testing
body:
## Overview
A dedicated sprint for triaging all bugs discovered during private beta, fixing them, and confirming regressions are resolved before public launch.

## Process
- Bugs are filed as separate GitHub issues tagged `bug` during beta testing
- This ticket tracks the triage and resolution process, not individual bugs

## Tasks
- [ ] Triage all bugs from beta feedback into: Critical (blocks launch), High (fix before launch), Medium (fix post-launch), Low (backlog)
- [ ] Resolve all Critical and High bugs
- [ ] Re-run end-to-end payment test scenarios from ticket #29 after bug fixes to confirm no regressions
- [ ] Run smoke tests across all four apps (API, web, mobile, admin) after final fix
- [ ] Get sign-off from at least one beta tester that their reported bug is resolved

## Acceptance criteria
- Zero Critical or High bugs remain open at the end of this ticket
- All payment flow test scenarios from #29 pass on the fixed codebase
- Beta testers confirm their key reported issues are resolved

title: Beta: Performance and load baseline testing
body:
## Overview
Establish baseline performance metrics before public launch so you have a reference point for detecting degradation as user numbers grow.

## Tasks
- [ ] Use k6 or Artillery to run a basic load test against the staging API
- [ ] Test key endpoints under load: `POST /auth/login`, `POST /payments/contribute/:cycleId`, `GET /groups/:id`, `POST /payments/webhook`
- [ ] Establish baseline: p95 response time, error rate at 100 concurrent users
- [ ] Identify any obvious N+1 query issues in Prisma (use `prisma.$queryRaw` logging or Prisma's query event)
- [ ] Set up basic uptime monitoring (Railway's built-in or BetterUptime) on the API `/health` endpoint
- [ ] Configure Sentry performance monitoring with transaction tracing on the API

## Acceptance criteria
- p95 response time for all key endpoints is under 500ms at 100 concurrent users
- Zero 5xx errors under baseline load
- Uptime monitoring is configured and sending alerts to a nominated Slack/email
- Sentry performance dashboard is live

title: Compliance: Engage a Nigerian fintech lawyer for regulatory review
body:
## Overview
Engage a lawyer with Nigerian fintech and CBN regulatory experience to advise on Poolr's licensing requirements, wallet structure, and data protection obligations before public launch.

## Topics to cover with legal counsel
- [ ] CBN licensing assessment: does Poolr's wallet model (holding customer funds between payout and withdrawal) require a PSP, PSSP, or other CBN license, or can it operate under Paystack's existing licenses as a platform?
- [ ] Paystack's terms of service: confirm Poolr's use case (rotating savings circles, wallet, transfers) is permitted under Paystack's platform terms
- [ ] Smile ID data handling: confirm BVN and NIN data handling complies with CBN KYC guidelines and the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA) 2023
- [ ] S3 document storage: confirm storing Nigerian government ID documents in AWS S3 (likely us-east-1) satisfies NDPA data residency considerations or advise on alternatives
- [ ] Penalty fees: confirm that charging a penalty fee for missed contributions is legally permissible and does not require additional licensing
- [ ] Transaction fee: confirm that charging a 1% fee on payouts is permissible under current CBN guidelines

## Deliverables expected from legal counsel
- A written legal opinion covering the above topics
- A list of any licenses to apply for before or shortly after public launch
- Draft terms of service and privacy policy (or review of internally drafted ones)

## Acceptance criteria
- Written legal opinion received and reviewed
- All identified licensing actions are filed as separate GitHub issues with deadlines
- Terms of service and privacy policy are drafted and reviewed by legal counsel

title: Compliance: Register with Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC)
body:
## Overview
Register Poolr as a data controller with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) as required under the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA) 2023.

## Tasks
- [ ] Confirm registration requirements and fee on the NDPC portal (ndpc.gov.ng)
- [ ] Prepare required documentation: company registration details, data processing activities summary, DPO (Data Protection Officer) appointment if required
- [ ] Complete NDPC registration and obtain Data Controller registration certificate
- [ ] Appoint or designate a Data Protection Officer (can be internal for a startup)
- [ ] Conduct a basic Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) covering BVN/NIN collection, ID document storage, and third-party data sharing (Smile ID, Paystack, Termii)
- [ ] Document data retention policies: how long KYC documents, transaction records, and user data are kept, and deletion procedures

## Acceptance criteria
- NDPC registration certificate obtained
- DPIA document completed and stored in company records
- Data retention policy documented and reflected in the privacy policy

title: Compliance: Draft and publish Terms of Service and Privacy Policy
body:
## Overview
Draft, have legally reviewed, and publish Poolr's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy before public launch.

## Tasks
- [ ] Draft Terms of Service covering: user eligibility, group rules, contribution obligations, penalty policy, Poolr's liability limits, wallet and withdrawal terms, account termination
- [ ] Draft Privacy Policy covering: what data is collected (BVN, NIN, phone, email, transaction history), why it is collected, who it is shared with (Smile ID, Paystack, Termii, Firebase, AWS), how long it is kept, user rights under NDPA
- [ ] Have both documents reviewed by legal counsel from ticket #32
- [ ] Add Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages to the web app
- [ ] Add acceptance checkbox to registration flow (users must accept ToS and Privacy Policy to create an account)
- [ ] Store acceptance timestamp and version number per user in the database
- [ ] Add `terms_accepted_at` and `terms_version` fields to `User` model

## Acceptance criteria
- Both documents are published at public URLs before any public-facing launch
- Registration flow requires explicit acceptance, not just a passive link
- Legal counsel has reviewed and signed off on both documents
- `terms_accepted_at` is recorded for every new user from launch onwards

title: Compliance: Security audit and penetration testing
body:
## Overview
Conduct a basic security audit of the Poolr API and infrastructure before public launch. This is especially critical given that the app handles KYC identity documents, BVN/NIN data, and real money transfers.

## Areas to audit
- [ ] JWT implementation: token expiry, refresh token rotation, revocation on logout
- [ ] Paystack webhook HMAC verification: confirm signature check cannot be bypassed
- [ ] Smile ID webhook: confirm webhook origin is validated
- [ ] S3 bucket permissions: confirm KYC document buckets are private, not publicly listable
- [ ] Prisma query safety: confirm no raw SQL injection vectors in any `$queryRaw` calls
- [ ] Rate limiting: confirm auth endpoints (login, OTP) are rate-limited to prevent brute force
- [ ] CORS configuration: confirm only permitted origins are whitelisted
- [ ] Environment variables: confirm no secrets are exposed in client-side bundles (Next.js public env vars)
- [ ] Dependency audit: run `pnpm audit` and resolve any high/critical vulnerabilities
- [ ] Consider engaging an external penetration testing service for a lightweight pentest

## Tasks
- [ ] Complete internal security checklist above
- [ ] Run `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` and resolve all high/critical findings
- [ ] Run OWASP ZAP or similar against the staging API for automated vulnerability scanning
- [ ] Document findings and resolutions

## Acceptance criteria
- All checklist items reviewed and documented
- Zero high or critical npm vulnerabilities in production dependencies
- S3 buckets confirmed private
- OWASP scan returns no high or critical findings

title: Launch: Build Poolr landing page
body:
## Overview
Build a public-facing marketing landing page for Poolr to drive signups, explain the product, and link to the app stores and web app.

## Sections
- Hero: headline, subheading, CTA ("Join the waitlist" or "Get started")
- How it works: 3-step explainer (Create a group, contribute each cycle, collect your payout)
- Features: key selling points (KYC-verified members, automated payouts, penalty protection, wallet)
- Testimonials: placeholder for beta tester quotes post-beta
- App store badges: iOS App Store and Google Play links
- Footer: links to Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, contact email

## Tasks
- [ ] Build landing page at `apps/web/app/(marketing)/page.tsx` or as a separate `apps/landing` Next.js app
- [ ] Use Poolr brand colors (#085041 primary, #EF9F27 accent) and the approved coin-ring logo mark
- [ ] Make fully responsive (mobile-first - most Nigerian users will land on mobile)
- [ ] Integrate a simple waitlist/signup form (Tally, or a lightweight `POST /waitlist` endpoint)
- [ ] Add SEO metadata: title, description, Open Graph image
- [ ] Deploy to production Vercel domain
- [ ] Set up Google Analytics or Plausible for basic traffic tracking

## Acceptance criteria
- Landing page is live at the production domain
- Page is fully responsive on mobile (375px) and desktop
- Waitlist form submissions are captured and stored
- Core Web Vitals scores: LCP under 2.5s, CLS under 0.1 on mobile

title: Launch: iOS App Store submission
body:
## Overview
Prepare and submit the Poolr iOS app to the Apple App Store via Expo EAS.

## Tasks
- [ ] Create an Apple Developer account (if not already done) - $99/year
- [ ] Configure `app.json` / `eas.json` in `apps/mobile` with correct bundle ID, version, and build number
- [ ] Generate and configure required App Store assets:
  - [ ] App icon: 1024x1024 PNG (no alpha, no rounded corners - Apple adds them)
  - [ ] Screenshots: at least 3 per device size (6.7", 6.1", 5.5" iPhone)
  - [ ] App preview video (optional but recommended)
- [ ] Write App Store listing copy: name ("Poolr"), subtitle, description, keywords, support URL, privacy policy URL
- [ ] Configure Expo EAS production build: `eas build --platform ios --profile production`
- [ ] Submit to App Store Connect: `eas submit --platform ios`
- [ ] Prepare for Apple review: ensure KYC, financial, and payment flows are clearly explained in the review notes
- [ ] Monitor review status - allow 1-3 business days for initial review
- [ ] Respond promptly to any Apple review questions or rejections

## Acceptance criteria
- App is approved and live on the iOS App Store
- All App Store screenshots show real app UI (not placeholder)
- Privacy policy URL is live and linked correctly in App Store Connect

## Note
Apple commonly rejects fintech apps for: missing privacy policy, unclear explanation of KYC/financial features, or test account not provided. Prepare a demo account for the reviewer with a pre-verified KYC status and a pre-created group.

title: Launch: Google Play Store submission
body:
## Overview
Prepare and submit the Poolr Android app to the Google Play Store via Expo EAS.

## Tasks
- [ ] Create a Google Play Developer account (if not already done) - $25 one-time fee
- [ ] Configure `app.json` / `eas.json` with correct Android package name, version code, and version name
- [ ] Generate and configure required Play Store assets:
  - [ ] App icon: 512x512 PNG
  - [ ] Feature graphic: 1024x500 PNG (required for Play Store listing)
  - [ ] Screenshots: at least 2 phone screenshots (16:9 or 9:16)
  - [ ] Android adaptive icon: foreground layer (use the `poolr-icon-android-adaptive-432.png` from the icon assets package)
- [ ] Write Play Store listing: title, short description (80 chars), full description, app category (Finance)
- [ ] Declare sensitive permissions in Play Console: camera (KYC selfie), storage (ID document upload)
- [ ] Complete Play Store data safety form: declare all data collected (name, email, phone, financial info, government ID) and data sharing (Paystack, Smile ID, Termii, Firebase)
- [ ] Configure Expo EAS production build: `eas build --platform android --profile production`
- [ ] Submit to Play Console: `eas submit --platform android`
- [ ] Set up internal testing track first, then promote to production after final validation

## Acceptance criteria
- App is approved and live on Google Play Store
- Data safety form is fully completed and accurate
- Adaptive icon renders correctly on all Android launcher shapes (circle, square, squircle, teardrop)

title: Launch: Set up production infrastructure and monitoring
body:
## Overview
Set up and harden the production environment on Railway and Vercel ahead of public launch.

## Tasks
- [ ] Create separate Railway production project (separate from staging)
- [ ] Configure production environment variables (live Paystack secret keys, live Smile ID credentials, live Termii keys)
- [ ] Enable Railway's automatic PostgreSQL backups (daily, 7-day retention minimum)
- [ ] Set up Redis persistence configuration on Railway (AOF or RDB snapshots)
- [ ] Configure production domain: custom domain on Vercel for web app, custom domain for API on Railway
- [ ] Set up SSL certificates (Vercel and Railway handle this automatically but confirm)
- [ ] Configure Sentry production environment with separate DSN from staging
- [ ] Set up uptime monitoring with alerting (BetterUptime or similar) on: API `/health`, web app, admin dashboard
- [ ] Configure Paystack live webhook endpoint and confirm HMAC secret is set correctly
- [ ] Set up Smile ID production credentials and confirm KYC webhook URL is pointing to production
- [ ] Run a final smoke test on production infrastructure with a test transaction before flipping traffic

## Acceptance criteria
- All production environment variables are set and confirmed working
- Daily DB backups are configured and verified (trigger a manual backup and confirm restore works)
- Uptime monitoring is alerting to a nominated email/Slack channel
- Sentry is capturing errors in the production environment
- Custom domains resolve correctly with valid SSL

title: Launch: Waitlist email campaign and launch announcement
body:
## Overview
Convert the waitlist built during the pre-launch period into active Poolr users with a launch email sequence and social media announcement.

## Tasks
- [ ] Write launch email sequence (3 emails via Resend):
  - Email 1: You're in - Poolr is live, here is how to get started
  - Email 2: 3 days later - how to create your first group
  - Email 3: 7 days later - invite your savings circle (referral prompt)
- [ ] Design email templates using React Email (consistent with Poolr brand colors)
- [ ] Segment waitlist by source if applicable (diaspora vs Nigeria, individual vs trader/corporate)
- [ ] Send launch email to full waitlist on launch day
- [ ] Prepare social media launch posts: Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Instagram, WhatsApp status
- [ ] Reach out to Nigerian fintech journalists and newsletters (Techpoint, Nairametrics, The Aza Report) with a press release or product brief
- [ ] Monitor signups and conversion rate from waitlist email open to completed registration in the 72 hours post-launch

## Acceptance criteria
- Launch email delivered to 100% of waitlist with under 2% bounce rate
- Conversion rate from waitlist email to completed registration is tracked
- At least one Nigerian tech media outlet covers or acknowledges the launch

title: Growth: Referral programme
body:
## Overview
Build a referral programme that rewards existing Poolr users with a wallet credit for every new verified user they refer who completes their first full contribution cycle.

## How it works
- Every user gets a unique referral code and shareable link on their profile
- When a new user signs up via a referral link, the referral is tracked
- When the referred user completes their first contribution in any group, the referrer receives a wallet credit (e.g. 500 NGN)
- The referred user optionally receives a welcome bonus too (e.g. 200 NGN wallet credit on first contribution)

## Schema changes
- [ ] Add `referral_code` (unique string) to `User` model
- [ ] Add `referred_by_id` (FK to User) to `User` model
- [ ] Add `Referral` table: id, referrer_id, referred_id, status (PENDING, REWARDED), rewarded_at

## API tasks
- [ ] Generate unique referral code on user creation (e.g. POOLR-ABCD1234)
- [ ] Accept `referral_code` as an optional param on `POST /auth/register`
- [ ] Create referral record on signup if a valid code is provided
- [ ] Trigger referral reward in `PaymentsService` when a referred user's first contribution is marked PAID:
  - Credit referrer wallet via `WalletService.credit()`
  - Credit referred user wallet (welcome bonus)
  - Update `Referral.status` to REWARDED
- [ ] Expose `GET /referrals` - list own referrals with status and earnings
- [ ] Write unit tests for referral reward logic

## Frontend tasks (web + mobile)
- [ ] Add referral section to user profile page: unique link, copy button, QR code
- [ ] Show referral history and total earnings from referrals
- [ ] Add referral code field to registration screen (auto-populated if arriving via referral link)

## Acceptance criteria
- Referrer receives wallet credit only after the referred user completes their first contribution (not on signup)
- A user cannot refer themselves (same email/phone check)
- Referral rewards are idempotent - no double crediting if events fire multiple times
- Referral earnings are clearly itemised in the wallet transaction history

title: Growth: Wallet interest sharing (float revenue share)
body:
## Overview
Share a portion of the interest earned on pooled wallet balances (float) with users whose money is sitting in the Poolr wallet. This rewards users for leaving payouts in the wallet rather than immediately withdrawing, and differentiates Poolr from competitors who keep 100% of float revenue.

## How it works
- Poolr earns interest on the aggregate balance held across all users' Poolr Wallets in its Paystack settlement account
- A configurable percentage of that interest is shared back with users proportional to their average daily wallet balance
- Interest is credited to users' wallets monthly as a "Poolr Interest" transaction
- The interest rate offered to users is lower than what Poolr earns (Poolr keeps a spread)

## Regulatory note
This feature MUST be reviewed by legal counsel (ticket #32) before going live. Paying interest on held funds may require additional CBN licensing. This ticket should be blocked on legal sign-off.

## Schema changes
- [ ] Add `InterestAccrual` table: id, user_id, period_start, period_end, avg_daily_balance, interest_rate, amount_credited, credited_at
- [ ] Add `INTEREST` as a new `WalletTransaction` type

## API tasks
- [ ] Create `InterestService` in the wallet module
- [ ] Daily cron job: snapshot each user's wallet balance into a daily balance log
- [ ] Monthly cron job: calculate average daily balance per user for the month, compute interest at the configured rate, credit wallet via `WalletService.credit()`, create `InterestAccrual` record
- [ ] Expose `GET /wallet/interest` - list interest accruals by month
- [ ] Add configurable interest rate to admin settings (start conservative: 4-6% annualised to users)

## Frontend tasks
- [ ] Show current interest rate on wallet screen ("Earn X% p.a. on your Poolr Wallet")
- [ ] Show monthly interest credited in wallet transaction history
- [ ] Add interest earnings summary to wallet screen (total earned this year)

## Acceptance criteria
- Interest is calculated correctly based on average daily balance, not just end-of-month snapshot
- Zero cases of interest being credited twice for the same period (idempotent monthly job)
- Legal sign-off obtained before feature goes live (see ticket #32)
- Interest rate is configurable without a code deploy (stored in DB or environment config)

title: Growth: Trust score system
body:
## Overview
Build a trust score system that rewards users for reliable contribution behaviour and unlocks perks as the score increases.

## How the score works
- Every user starts with a base trust score of 50
- Score increases for: on-time contributions (+5 per cycle), completing a full group cycle (+20), receiving no penalties in a cycle (+3)
- Score decreases for: missed contribution (-15), late contribution (-5), penalty waived by admin (no change - neutral)
- Score is capped between 0 and 100
- Score is visible to the user and optionally visible to group admins when reviewing membership requests

## Perks unlocked by trust score
- 0-39 (New): Standard - can join groups up to 10 members, no preferred rotation position
- 40-59 (Trusted): Can join groups up to 20 members, reduced penalty fee (50% discount)
- 60-79 (Reliable): Can join groups up to 50 members, eligible for early rotation position preference
- 80-100 (Elite): Unlimited group size, zero platform fees on one group per month, priority payout scheduling

## Schema changes
- [ ] Add `trust_score` (int, default 50) to `User` model
- [ ] Add `TrustScoreEvent` table: id, user_id, event_type, points_delta, reason, created_at

## API tasks
- [ ] Create `TrustScoreService`
- [ ] Trigger score update events from: `PaymentsService` (on-time vs late contribution), `PenaltyService` (missed contribution), `GroupsService` (cycle completion)
- [ ] Expose `GET /users/me/trust-score` - current score, tier, and recent score events
- [ ] Factor trust score into group join eligibility checks in `GroupsService`

## Frontend tasks
- [ ] Add trust score badge to user profile (show tier name and score)
- [ ] Show score history with event descriptions ("On-time contribution +5", "Missed contribution -15")
- [ ] Show locked and unlocked perks per tier

## Acceptance criteria
- Score updates are triggered correctly by all relevant events
- Score never goes below 0 or above 100
- Group join is blocked with a clear message if trust score is below the group's minimum (if admin has set one)
- Trust score events are always logged to `TrustScoreEvent` for auditability

title: Growth: B2B cooperative and corporate group onboarding
body:
## Overview
Build a lightweight B2B onboarding flow for corporate HR teams and large market cooperatives who want to run Ajo groups for their members/employees at scale.

## What B2B adds over the standard product
- A verified "Organisation" entity that owns and manages multiple groups
- Bulk member import (CSV upload of employee/member list)
- Organisation-level admin dashboard showing all groups, total pooled, and payout schedule across groups
- Custom branding option (organisation logo on group invite emails)
- Flat monthly fee billing instead of per-transaction fee (negotiated per organisation)

## Schema changes
- [ ] Add `Organisation` table: id, name, logo_url, contact_email, billing_type (TRANSACTION_FEE, FLAT_MONTHLY), monthly_fee, created_at
- [ ] Add `organisation_id` (optional FK) to `Group` model
- [ ] Add `ORG_ADMIN` to `Role` enum

## API tasks
- [ ] `POST /organisations` - create organisation (super admin only)
- [ ] `POST /organisations/:id/members/import` - bulk import members via CSV (name, email, phone)
- [ ] `GET /organisations/:id/dashboard` - aggregate stats across all groups
- [ ] Adjust fee calculation to use flat monthly billing for organisation-owned groups

## Frontend tasks (admin dashboard)
- [ ] Organisation overview page: all groups, total members, total pooled this month
- [ ] Bulk member import UI: CSV upload with preview and validation before import
- [ ] Organisation settings: logo upload, contact info, billing type

## Sales tasks
- [ ] Identify 5-10 target organisations for B2B pilot: market cooperatives (Alaba, Balogun, Computer Village), corporate HR teams (mid-size Lagos companies)
- [ ] Prepare a one-page B2B product brief explaining Poolr for organisations
- [ ] Set up a B2B inquiry form on the landing page

## Acceptance criteria
- An organisation admin can import 50+ members via CSV and create a group for them without manually inviting each member
- Organisation dashboard shows accurate aggregate stats across all groups
- Flat monthly billing is calculated correctly and applied to organisation-owned groups

title: Growth: Diaspora acquisition campaign
body:
## Overview
Launch a targeted user acquisition campaign aimed at the Nigerian diaspora in the UK, US, and Canada - a high-value segment with larger contribution amounts and high familiarity with Susu/Ajo savings circles.

## Why diaspora first
- Average contribution amounts likely 3-5x higher than Nigeria-based groups (NGN equivalent of GBP/USD contributions)
- Diaspora communities already run informal Susu groups via WhatsApp and cash - a digital solution directly replaces an existing painful workflow
- Paystack supports NGN payments for diaspora users with Nigerian bank accounts
- Word-of-mouth in tight diaspora communities is extremely efficient for trust-based financial products

## Tasks
- [ ] Confirm Paystack's support for diaspora users (Nigerian bank account holders outside Nigeria) and document any limitations
- [ ] Create diaspora-specific landing page variant: messaging focused on "run your Susu group digitally, safely, from anywhere"
- [ ] Identify and reach out to Nigerian diaspora community groups: Nigerian Union UK chapters, NANS diaspora, Nigerian community Facebook groups in London/Houston/Toronto
- [ ] Partner with 2-3 diaspora community leaders or influencers for a pilot group (offer fee-free first cycle)
- [ ] Create WhatsApp-shareable explainer card for how Poolr works (visual, short, shareable)
- [ ] Track diaspora vs Nigeria-based signups and contribution amounts separately in analytics

## Acceptance criteria
- At least 2 diaspora groups complete a full cycle within 60 days of campaign launch
- Average contribution amount for diaspora groups is tracked and reported
- Referral rate (how many new users each diaspora user invites) is tracked

title: Growth: In-app group chat
body:
## Overview
Add a simple in-app group chat to each Ajo group, preserving the social glue that makes Ajo work in real life. Chat is scoped per group - members can only see messages from their own group.

## How it works
- Each group has its own chat thread
- All group members (including admin) can send and receive messages
- Automated system messages appear in the chat for key events: cycle started, contribution received, payout sent, penalty applied
- Chat is not a general social feed - it is strictly tied to each group

## Technical approach
- Use Firebase Realtime Database or Firestore for chat (avoids building WebSocket infrastructure on NestJS from scratch)
- Store message metadata (sender, timestamp, group_id) in Firestore; no need to mirror to PostgreSQL
- Firebase FCM (already integrated) handles push notifications for new messages when app is backgrounded

## Tasks
- [ ] Set up Firestore collection structure: `groups/{groupId}/messages/{messageId}`
- [ ] Create `ChatService` on the backend that writes system messages to Firestore on key events
- [ ] Web: build chat UI component in the group detail page (message list + input)
- [ ] Mobile: build chat screen in the group detail tab
- [ ] Implement real-time message subscription (Firestore `onSnapshot` listener)
- [ ] Push notification for new chat messages when app is backgrounded
- [ ] Moderation: admin can delete any message in their group

## Acceptance criteria
- Messages appear in real time for all group members without page refresh
- System messages appear automatically when contribution is confirmed or payout is sent
- Push notification fires within 5 seconds of a new message for backgrounded users
- Admin can delete inappropriate messages
